items.video_title: Engine Knock Sound When Accelerating? Here's Why
items.video_description:
Engine knock, or pinging, is an abnormal combustion event often heard during acceleration, caused by factors like low-octane fuel, incorrect ignition timing, lean air-fuel mixtures, faulty sensors, or carbon buildup. Diagnosing it involves checking for trouble codes, inspecting ignition components, analyzing fuel trims and timing data, verifying sensor accuracy, and assessing mechanical health through compression or borescope tests. Common fixes include using higher-octane fuel, replacing spark plugs or sensors, cleaning the intake system, and correcting ECU timing. Preventing knock requires regular maintenance, using the right fuel, and avoiding engine lugging under load.

items.video_title: I Tried Sketchy Used Car Lot Tricks to Hide Engine Knock
items.video_description:
Used car lots have a reputation for hiding engine problems, so I decided to test some of the sketchiest tricks ever used to quiet a knocking engine.

From thick oil additives to mystery fixes and finally sawdust in the engine, I tested what actually works — and how dangerous these tricks really are.

If you’re buying a used car or diagnosing engine knock, you NEED to see this.

⚠️ This video is for educational purposes only. Do not try these methods on a vehicle you care about.

Subscribe for real-world automotive testing, engine diagnostics, and exposing shady car myths.

But Unlike Manuals And Rear End Gears I Just Figured Sawdust Would  Plug The Filter . Yes I Know Like The Oil Filter In The Engine. ​@Chann3Lsurf3R825Man I Forgot All About That. My Daughter'S Favorite Movie For A Couple Of Years 😂 It Will Also Quiet Top End Lifter Clatter... Adding Aluminum Foil To The Bearing Is The Old Used Car Lot Trick.  It Works Long Enough To Blame The Customer. The Sawdust Was For Noisy Rear Ends And Standard Transmissions.  Also Back When Mobil 1 Was Really Pao Based Oil, Car Lots Would Use It To Stop A Smoking Engine. Even New Car Dealers Would Do It To Auction A Smoker Off To The Buy Here Die Here Lots That Was Really Common In The 80S And 90S. This Is Actually Hilarious, I Once Pulled Apart A Slant6 And Found Aluminum Flashing Wedged In A Rod Bearing. Surprisingly It Was Not Making Any Noise, So It Clearly Did The Job Of Shimming It. " The Sawdust Was For Noisy Rear Ends And Standard Transmissions."  Thank You, Never Heard If It Dumped Into An Engine, The Filter And Pump Screen Would Be Blocked.....
I Think This Was Made Popular By That Andy Grffith Show Where Barney Got Ripped Off On A Used Car... Yeah That'S What I Always Heard As A Young Mechanic.....😅 If Bothered To Pull Apart The Motor To Add The Foil Why Not Just Replace The Bearing? @Buddythewolfyt No Sir, This Was Aluminum Flashing. Not Foil, And It Looked As If They Just Removed The Single Rod Cap And Put It In There. I Had That Thing A Long Time And Had No Idea It Was Down There, So It Did Exactly What They Intended It To. My Guess Is Maybe It Was Making Noise So They Pulled The Pan And Did That. I Dont Honestly Know As I Go Tit That Way. But It Clearly Worked. Sawdust Is Most Certainly Just An Old Urban Legend Because It Will Clog Oil Passages And In No Way Quiet Down The Knock.  Even The Shadiest Used Car Dealer Would Know From Word Of Mouth What Works And What Doesn'T. It Was Only Used In Rear Diffs In My Experience. Though I Have Read Manual Trans Too. ​@Joew8440Yep It Was Really Common Here In The [Plate Redacted]/40 Year Ago To Put It In The Rear Diff Of A Ford Cortina To Quieten It Down Sawdust Just Gums Up In A Motor But It Will Quiet Down Worn Differentials And Manual Transmissions For Awhile. That’S A True Thing I Believe Spawned The Myth Of Sawdust In The Engine I’Ve Even Heard Of People Shoving Bananas In Rear Ends You Never Had Rod Knock That’S Piston Slap, 4.0S Are Notorious For Cracked Pistons And Broken Skirts. $170 For Sealed Power Pistons And You Are Back On The Road. I Thought The Same Thing 😂 Don'T They Run With Little To No Hot Oil Pressure All The Time This Guy Really Bothers Me When He Runs Down Great Engines. Loud Tappy Knock Under 4000 Rpm But Ran Fine. Considering My Experience With This Engine, And The Fact That It Held Together I Think You Likely Have A Broken Piston/Piston Skirt, And Not A Bearing Problem.  I Have Heard Of Sawdust In Rear Ends And Manual Transmissions. But Wouldn'T Think Sawdust Could Get By The Oilpump Pickup Screen Would Think It Would Stop It Up  Had An Engine Guy Tell Me He Has Seen Rod Or Main Bearings Replaced With Leather From A Belt. Said You Could Not Tell It Was Messed Up For A While And It Actually Held Together. Close The Plug Gap To Stop That Cylinder From Firing, Takes The Pressure Off The Bearing, Pass It Off As 'Just Needs A Tune Up' Model T’S Used Leather Bearings From The Factory . Guys Would Service Them On The Side Of The Road . Couldn'T Amigine Being Right At Bearing To Not Replace It Tho Huh, Instead Of Putting All Back Together For Nothing Yeah, I Came Here To Say This. It Would Be A Pretty Crappy Thing To Do To Someone. Works Ok On Old Engines With A Compression Ratio Less Than 8:1. Anything Modern Just Pounds The Leather Out Quick.
